input.security: {"score": 48, "summary": "The most critical finding is a SQL injection vulnerability in RatingTrait where Auth::id() is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string. Several \"not equal to null\" comparisons use SQL syntax that is semantically incorrect (should be IS NOT NULL). The policy layer is well-structured and role-based, but the raw HTML generation in ratingAvgHtml() is unescaped.", "findings": [{"id": "SEC-001", "severity": "critical", "category": "security", "title": "SQL Injection via Auth::id() string interpolation in raw query", "description": "In RatingTrait::ratingObjectives(), Auth::id() is directly interpolated into a selectRaw() string: `sum(if(user_id=\"'.$user_id.'\",value,0))`. If the user ID value originates from an untrusted source or a manipulated session, this is a direct SQL injection vector. The sibling implementation in HasRatingsTrait correctly uses a parameterised placeholder (?), proving the safe pattern is known.", "file": "app/Models/Traits/RatingTrait.php", "line": 45, "snippet": "sum(if(user_id=\"'.$user_id.'\"  ,value,0)) AS rating_my", "fix": "Replace string interpolation with a parameterised binding, mirroring HasRatingsTrait:\n->selectRaw('sum(if(user_id = ?, value, 0)) AS rating_my', [$user_id])"}}, {"id": "SEC-002", "severity": "high", "category": "security", "title": "Incorrect NULL comparison produces wrong SQL (security + correctness)", "description": "Multiple locations use ->where('user_id', '!=', null) and ->wherePivot('user_id', '!=', null). Laravel/PDO translates this to `user_id != NULL` which always evaluates to UNKNOWN in SQL, meaning no rows are ever filtered as intended. The correct SQL is `user_id IS NOT NULL`. This silently skips the user filter, potentially leaking anonymous/system records into user-scoped queries.", "file": "app/Models/Traits/HasRating.php", "line": 95, "snippet": "->where('user_id', '!=', null)", "fix": "Replace all occurrences with ->whereNotNull('user_id') and ->wherePivotNotNull('user_id') respectively."}, {"id": "SEC-003", "severity": "medium", "category": "security", "title": "Unescaped model data rendered as raw HTML in ratingAvgHtml()", "description": "RatingTrait::ratingAvgHtml() and HasRatingsTrait::ratingAvgHtml() concatenate $this->title and numeric values directly into HTML button attributes without escaping. An XSS payload in a stored title (e.g. containing quotes) can break out of the attribute context.", "file": "app/Models/Traits/RatingTrait.php", "line": 165, "snippet": "$title = 'Vota '.$this->title;\n$btn = '...data-title=\"'.$title.'\"...'", "fix": "Use htmlspecialchars($title, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') when embedding values in HTML attribute strings, or refactor to Blade views which auto-escape."}]}

quality.summary: The codebase has significant code duplication across multiple trait files that implement near-identical logic, two conflicting RatingData classes in different namespaces, and dead/commented-out debug code. The dependency constraint '*' for spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes is dangerously unconstrained.

findings.title: Duplicate RatingData classes in two namespaces
findings.description: Two separate RatingData classes exist: Modules\Rating\DataObjects\RatingData (app/DataObjects/RatingData.php) and Modules\Rating\Datas\RatingData (app/Datas/RatingData.php). They have different constructors, different fields, and different validation logic. This creates confusion about which DTO to use, risks divergent evolution, and violates DRY.
findings.snippet:
namespace Modules\Rating\DataObjects;
final readonly class RatingData
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single canonical DTO (preferably the Spatie Data one in Datas/) and delete the other. Update all consumers.

findings.title: HasRatingsTrait and RatingTrait are near-identical duplicates
findings.description: RatingTrait (178 lines) and HasRatingsTrait (285 lines) implement the same public interface: ratings(), myRatings(), ratingObjectives(), scopeWithRating(), getRatingsAvgAttribute(), getRatingsCountAttribute(), ratingAvgHtml(). This dual-trait pattern guarantees divergence — the SQL injection in SEC-001 exists only in RatingTrait because fixes were applied to HasRatingsTrait but not propagated.
findings.fix: Deprecate and remove RatingTrait entirely. All consumers should use HasRatingsTrait (or HasRating for the pivot-based variant).

findings.title: RatingTable and BaseRatingsTable are byte-for-byte duplicates
findings.description: RatingTable (74 lines) and BaseRatingsTable (75 lines) define identical getTableColumns(), getTableFilters(), getTableActions() and getTableBulkActions() implementations. RatingTable does not extend BaseRatingsTable — it re-implements the same logic from scratch against the same base class.
findings.snippet: class RatingTable extends XotBaseResourceTable { ... identical body ... }
findings.fix: Make RatingTable extend BaseRatingsTable and delete the duplicated method bodies, overriding only what differs.

findings.title: Getter accessor triggers DB write (hidden side-effect)
findings.description: getRatingsAvgAttribute() and getRatingsCountAttribute() in both HasRatingsTrait and RatingTrait call $this->update([...]) inside a getter. Calling $model->ratings_avg or $model->ratings_count silently fires a DB UPDATE. This is a serious violation of the principle of least astonishment and can cause unintended writes in read-only contexts, loops, or when the model is constructed for display only.
findings.fix: Move the denormalisation into a dedicated service or a dedicated Eloquent observer/event listener triggered on rating creation, not in a read accessor.

findings.title: Dead code and debug artefacts left in production files
findings.description: Multiple files contain commented-out dddx() debug calls, unused commented code blocks, and TODO-style stubs (e.g. BaseCreateRating.php lines 14-21 with dddx references; HasLikes.php with 'Undocumented function'; RatingTrait lines 134-138 with commented-out setMyRatingAttribute containing dddx).
findings.fix: Remove all commented-out debug calls and dead code blocks. Enable a linter rule (e.g. phpmd UnusedCode) to prevent recurrence.

performance.summary: The N+1 query pattern is present in the StatsOverview widget which fires two separate Action calls per rating inside a loop. Accessor-triggered DB writes add unexpected write overhead on reads. The getRatingsPercentageByUser() method executes two separate COUNT queries per rating option inside a loop.

findings.title: N+1 queries in StatsOverview widget
findings.description: StatsOverview::getStats() iterates over all ratings for a record and calls GetSumByModelRatingIdAction and GetCountByModelRatingIdAction separately for each rating. Each action fires an independent DB query. For a record with N ratings, this emits 2N+2 queries on every widget render with no caching.
findings.fix: Replace individual per-rating queries with a single aggregated GROUP BY query: RatingMorph::where('model_id', $record->id)->whereNotNull('user_id')->groupBy('rating_id')->selectRaw('rating_id, SUM(value) as total, COUNT(*) as cnt')->get(). Populate all stats from this single result.

findings.title: N+1 queries in getRatingsPercentageByUser()
findings.description: HasRating::getRatingsPercentageByUser() runs two COUNT(*) queries (one for total, one filtered by rating_id) per entry in $ratings_options, all inside a foreach loop. For a post with K rating options this emits 2K database round trips.
findings.fix: Replace the loop with a single GROUP BY query: RatingMorph::where('model_id', $this->id)->whereNotNull('user_id')->groupBy('rating_id')->selectRaw('rating_id, COUNT(*) as cnt')->get(). Compute percentages in PHP from that result set.

findings.title: Accessor side-effect causes redundant UPDATE on every read
findings.description: When ratings_avg or ratings_count is not already set as a column value, the accessor recomputes it by loading the full ratings relation and immediately issues an UPDATE. In a list view or loop over N models, this causes N lazy loads + N UPDATEs, dramatically increasing DB load.
findings.fix: Use a database-level trigger or an Eloquent observer on RatingMorph saved/deleted events to maintain denormalised counts, keeping reads pure.

architecture.summary: The module applies a reasonable layered pattern (Models, Actions, Filament Resources, Providers) and uses abstract base classes for extensibility. However, structural problems undermine this: three traits covering nearly identical ground, four migration files that create the same ratings table, two conflicting DTO namespaces, and wildcard composer constraints all point to evolutionary drift without governance.

findings.title: Four overlapping migrations targeting the same ratings table
findings.description: Four migration files (2023_01_01_000000, 2026_03_12, 2026_06_16 — plus the morph addendum pair) all create or alter the same `ratings` table. The 2023 and 2026 migrations share almost identical CREATE blocks. Running all migrations in order on a fresh install will execute redundant tableCreate/tableUpdate cycles. This creates hidden ordering dependencies and makes the schema history unreadable.
findings.snippet: // 4th migration file targeting the same 'ratings' table
findings.fix: Squash the ratings table migrations into a single canonical migration. Use the tableUpdate idempotent pattern only for genuinely additive changes introduced after the initial release.

findings.title: Three parallel trait implementations for the same HasRating concern
findings.description: HasRating, HasRatingsTrait, and RatingTrait all expose a ratings() relationship and supporting query methods on the consuming model. There is no clear ownership or deprecation path, and all three are live (PHPStan suppressions indicate awareness but no resolution). Consumers in external modules have no guidance on which to use.
findings.fix: Define a single canonical trait (HasRating, backed by the pivot-aware implementation). Formally deprecate HasRatingsTrait and RatingTrait with @deprecated docblocks and a migration guide in CHANGELOG.

findings.title: Wildcard (*) version constraint for spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes
findings.description: composer.json requires 'spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes': '*'. A wildcard constraint allows any version including major breaking releases to be installed, which can silently break schemaless attribute casting across the entire module without notice.
findings.fix: Pin to a specific semver range, e.g. "^1.9" or "^2.0" matching the currently installed version. Apply the same discipline to transitive Xot/Tenant/UI path dependencies.

findings.title: Media conversion named '50x50' produces 150x150 dimensions
findings.description: BaseRating::registerMediaConversions() defines a conversion named '50x50' but sets width(150)->height(150). The name and the actual dimensions are mismatched, which will silently deliver incorrectly sized images to consumers expecting 50x50 thumbnails.
findings.fix: Either rename the conversion to '150x150' or set the correct dimensions ->width(50)->height(50) to match the declared name.

testing.summary: The static analyser already flagged the absence of runnable tests. All Feature tests are unconditionally skipped via beforeEach(skip(...)). Unit tests exist but reference wrong table names and wrong DB connections. No integration, policy, or trait behavioural tests are present for the core rating logic.

findings.title: All Feature tests are permanently skipped
findings.description: RatingApiTest.php wraps every test in a beforeEach that calls skip(). The tests are syntactically present but will never execute. This gives false confidence in CI — the test suite passes because all tests are skipped, not because the code is correct.
findings.fix: Either remove the tests entirely until the routes exist, or implement proper route registration in the test environment and remove the skip() call. Use ->markTestIncomplete() in individual tests if partially ready.

findings.title: Unit test references wrong table name for rating_morph
findings.description: RatingTest.php asserts against DB::connection('rating')->table('rating_morphs') (line 47, pluralised), but the model and migration explicitly define the table as 'rating_morph' (singular). This test would always fail if actually executed.
findings.fix: Change 'rating_morphs' to 'rating_morph' to match the actual table name defined in BaseRatingMorph::$table.

findings.title: No tests for core security-sensitive logic (policy, trait filtering)
findings.description: There are no tests covering RatingPolicy or RatingMorphPolicy, the HasRating::getRatingsPercentageByUser() N+1 path, or the accessor-triggered UPDATE side effect. The SEC-001 SQL injection in RatingTrait has no regression test preventing reintroduction.
findings.fix: Add Pest tests for: (1) each policy method with role fixtures, (2) getRatingsPercentageByUser() asserting correct SQL/result without N+1, (3) a regression test confirming Auth::id() is never directly interpolated into raw SQL.

documentation.summary: The module has unusually extensive documentation (80+ markdown files in docs/) covering architecture, roadmaps, sprint plans, and PHPStan fixes. However, this volume creates its own problem: duplicated, outdated, and contradictory documents make it hard to find the authoritative reference. Core public APIs (traits, actions) have minimal inline docblocks.

findings.title: Excessive duplicate documentation files obscure authoritative content
findings.description: The docs/ folder contains multiple files covering the same topics with slight variations: CHANGELOG.md / changelog.md / docs/CHANGELOG.md / docs/changelog.md; LICENSE.md / license.md / docs/LICENSE.md / docs/license.md; duplicate-methods-analysis.md / duplicate_methods.md / duplicate_methods_report.md; copilot-redundancy-audit.md / copilot-redundancy-audit-2026-05-25.md. This document sprawl means consumers cannot identify the canonical reference.
findings.fix: Apply the docs-archive-policy.md (which already exists) rigorously: keep one CHANGELOG.md at root, archive or delete superseded analysis files, and enforce a single docs/index.md as the entry point.

findings.title: Public trait methods lack meaningful docblocks
findings.description: Key public methods in HasRating, HasRatingsTrait, and RatingTrait have either missing or stub docblocks ('Undocumented function', '----.', empty). External module consumers who use these traits have no inline guidance on expected inputs, return shapes, or side effects (especially the hidden DB-write side effect in the accessor).
findings.snippet: public function getBettingUsers(): int { ... } // no docblock
findings.fix: Add @param, @return, and @throws docblocks to all public methods. Explicitly document the DB write side-effect on getRatingsAvgAttribute and getRatingsCountAttribute with a @sideEffect note.

findings.title: README describes wrong test command path
findings.description: README.md instructs users to run tests but the actual test configuration (Pest, TestCase extending module-specific base) requires specific setup that is not documented. The Feature tests are all skipped, so following the README gives a misleadingly green result.
findings.snippet: // README test instructions don't reflect skipped-test reality
findings.fix: Update README to note which test suites are currently enabled vs. skipped, and document any required .env or DB connection (rating connection) setup for local test runs.

dependencies.summary: The wildcard constraint on spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes is the primary risk. The module uses minimum-stability: dev which further compounds version instability. Path-based repositories for Xot, Tenant, and UI mean this module cannot be installed independently, creating tight coupling that is invisible to standard dependency tooling.

findings.title: Wildcard version constraint allows any breaking version of schemaless-attributes
findings.description: composer.json specifies "spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes": "*". Combined with "minimum-stability": "dev", this will accept any alpha, beta, or major version of the package. A major version bump with API changes will silently break all SchemalessAttributes casts across the module.
findings.fix: Pin to a specific caret range matching the currently installed version: "spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes": "^2.0". Run composer show spatie/laravel-schemaless-attributes to find the installed version.

findings.title: minimum-stability: dev makes all transitive dependencies unstable
findings.description: Setting minimum-stability to 'dev' globally allows Composer to pull in dev/alpha releases for any transitive dependency, not just the ones you explicitly require. Combined with prefer-stable: true this is partially mitigated but still risky for a production module.
findings.fix: Set minimum-stability to 'stable' if possible. If specific dev-branch dependencies are needed, use inline stability flags (e.g., "some/package": "dev-main as 1.0.0") rather than lowering the global floor.

findings.title: Path-based repository coupling prevents standalone installation
findings.description: composer.json declares three path repositories (../Xot, ../Tenant, ../UI). This means the module can only be installed when those sibling directories exist at exactly those relative paths. It cannot be required via Packagist or in isolation, making CI, testing, and third-party adoption significantly harder.
findings.fix: Publish Xot, Tenant, and UI to a private Composer repository (e.g., Satis or Private Packagist) and replace path repositories with versioned package requirements. This decouples the installation from filesystem layout.

findings.title: Dual build toolchain (webpack.mix.js + vite.config.js) creates ambiguity
findings.description: Both webpack.mix.js (Laravel Mix) and vite.config.js (Vite) are present. Running the wrong build command produces a different asset pipeline. package.json scripts only reference mix commands, making vite.config.js effectively dead but potentially confusing contributors.
findings.fix: Decide on one build toolchain. If migrating to Vite, update package.json scripts and remove webpack.mix.js. If staying on Mix, remove vite.config.js.
